# WO-2026-08-10-16 — The shop owns the list, not the date
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

### The schema contradicts itself, and Warwick's shop pays for it

**`asdair.shop.list_id` has said the shop owns the list since migration 006. `unique (household_id,
list_date)` on `asdair.shopping_lists` says the DATE owns it.** Both cannot be true, and the
disagreement is what put an item from a cancelled week into Warwick's real shop on 2026-08-10.

WP-B15-07 fixed shop identity by grounding it in the inbound message. **The same fix cannot be
applied one layer down**, because at the list layer the date IS the identity, by schema — a second
list row for the same household and date is refused by Postgres whatever status it carries, since
the index does not include status.

**Silas's decision packet is the specification for this order:**
`Deliverables/2026-08-10-silas-shopping-lists-identity-decision.md`. Read it in full. It states the
recommended shape, the alternatives it rejected and why, the backfill rule, the consumers that
break, and the proof route. **You implement it; you do not re-litigate it.** If you believe it is
wrong, STOP and say so rather than quietly deviating.

**An interim mitigation already ships** (WP-B15-10, on `main`): the working set excludes list items
provably claimed by another shop. It closes the dead-shop case and does NOT close AC1's literal
wording — two live shops still share one list row, so a name present in both is one row and the
later write wins. **This order is the durable fix underneath that interim. Do not remove the
interim.**

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — MIGRATION 019, EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED.** Forward-only. Per Silas: add nullable
`shop_id bigint references asdair.shop(id)`; backfill from the existing `shop.list_id` link with
**the LIVE shop winning any shared row**; `unique (shop_id) where shop_id is not null`; preserve the
shop-less lane as `unique (household_id, list_date) where shop_id is null`; re-add
`(household_id, list_date)` as a plain index; then drop the original auto-named constraint **by
discovery**, not by a guessed name.

**AC2 — THE BACKFILL RULE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A TIE-BREAK.** The live shop must win a shared row.
Silas's reason, which you must preserve: giving a shared row to the earliest shop would strand the
live shop's already-materialised items behind the `shop_line.list_item_id` replay guard. **Encode
the reason in a comment, not just the behaviour.**

**AC3 — NOT ONE ROW IS MOVED, REWRITTEN OR ORPHANED**, and **no `shopping_list_items` row changes its
`list_id`**. This runs against Warwick's real household data. Prove it, do not assert it.

**AC4 — THE `(list_id, lower(item_name))` UPSERT IS LEFT BYTE-IDENTICAL.** Silas established it is
**not a database constraint at all** — no unique index exists on `shopping_list_items`; it is
`select … for update` under an advisory lock. **Do NOT add a unique index there**: it can fail to
build on pre-existing duplicate rows and would block the migration. Your change should finally make
its idempotency claim TRUE without touching the statement.

**AC5 — PROVEN AGAINST REAL POSTGRES, BECAUSE THE DOUBLE CANNOT PROVE IT.** `fakePg` models no
uniqueness on `shopping_lists` and its positional insert regex **will stop matching once `shop_id`
is added** — so an offline green here would be worthless twice over. Extend
`add-list-item.dbtest.mjs` per Silas §8: it currently applies `001` only, and the FK needs `006`
plus `019`. Deliver his seven named assertions, of which **(d) — same item name, same date, two shop
ids, two independent rows — is the one that actually proves the defect closed.**

**AC6 — THE NAMED CONSUMERS.** `skill/data.js:213-216` is the one genuinely breaking read —
`LIMIT 1` with no `ORDER BY`. Fix it. `add_regular_to_next_week` in `asdairCommands.mjs` would land
cockpit taps on a different list from the live shop; Silas calls this a **safe-default fix, not a
Warwick decision** — make it, and state what default you chose and why.

**AC7 — REPORT, DO NOT FIX:** `run-proofs.mjs:365,465-468,510,537` hard-code `shopping_lists <= 1`.
Outside your surface. Name the lines and what they will do after 019.

**AC8 — THE MIGRATION IS NOT APPLIED TO ANY LIVE DATABASE BY YOU.** `live_authority: none`. You write
it and prove it in the dbtest harness against a throwaway `postgres:16`. **Applying it to Warwick's
real store is a separate gated action that belongs to Larry and Warwick.** Say plainly in your
return that it is unapplied.

**AC9 — REGRESSION AND MUTATION.** The dbtest assertions ARE the regression: show assertion (d)
failing against the schema WITHOUT `019` and passing with it. Mutate the backfill's live-wins rule
and prove a NAMED assertion fails. **Assert the source actually changed before trusting any red** —
three workers hit silent no-op mutations in this build.

## Required evidence

- the extended `add-list-item.dbtest.mjs` against a real throwaway `postgres:16`, with 001 + 006 + 019 applied -> report each of Silas's seven assertions BY NAME with pass/fail, and the executed count
- the SAME dbtest against 001 + 006 WITHOUT 019 -> assertion (d) must FAIL. That is the regression.
- `cd services/asdair/skill && node --test` -> counts before and after (baseline 333)
- `cd services/asdair/pipeline && node --test` -> counts before and after (baseline 444)
- the AC9 mutation: named assertion RED, sha256 before and after restore, byte-identical
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/db/019_shopping_list_shop_identity.sql services/control-plane/wp-d-proof/asdairCommands.mjs services/control-plane/wp-d-proof/add-list-item.dbtest.mjs services/asdair/skill/data.js` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

- `services/asdair/db/001_asdair_schema.sql:251` — the constraint being replaced.
- `services/asdair/db/006_shop_control_surface.sql` — where `shop.list_id` already says the shop owns the list.
- `services/control-plane/wp-d-proof/asdairCommands.mjs:34-42` `findOrCreateDraftList` — the selection that returns the dead list.
- `services/asdair/pipeline/shopLines.js` — the WP-B15-10 interim this order sits underneath. **READ-ONLY, and do not remove the interim.**
- `services/asdair/pipeline/test/fakePg.js:1035-1049` — why the offline double cannot prove this. **READ-ONLY; another worker is live in that file.**

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- APPLYING the migration to any live database. Absolutely not (AC8).
- Adding a unique index to `shopping_list_items` (AC4). It can fail to build on existing duplicates and would block the migration.
- Removing WP-B15-10's interim exclusion rule.
- `run-proofs.mjs` — report only (AC7).
- THREE other workers are live: `pipeline/runPipeline.js` + `stages.js` + `handoff/completion.js`; `skill/termMatch.js` + `interpret/resolveByCatalogue.js`; `pipeline/runtime.js` + `test/fakePg.js`. **Note `skill/data.js` is yours but `skill/termMatch.js` is NOT.**
- Re-litigating Silas's schema shape. Implement it, or STOP and say why it is wrong.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK FIRST, then HOLD** (SOP-022). Confirm you have read Silas's packet, restate the
   migration shape in your own words, and name anything in it you believe is wrong. Do not implement
   until Larry accepts or amends.
2. Establish the dbtest harness can actually run here — a real `postgres:16` — BEFORE writing the
   migration. If it cannot, STOP and say so: an offline green is worthless for this change and I
   will not accept one.
3. Assertion (d) RED against 001+006 without 019. That is the regression and it comes first.
4. Write `019`. Then the consumers (AC6).
5. AC9 mutation on the backfill's live-wins rule.
6. Re-run both suites; report counts.
7. **Git endpoint: COMMIT and PUSH `build-015/b15-16-migration-019`. No PR. Do NOT touch `main`. Do
   NOT merge. Do NOT apply.**

Return: Silas's seven assertions by name with results, the (d)-without-019 regression, the mutation
pair, suite counts, what default you chose for `add_regular_to_next_week` and why, the
`run-proofs.mjs` lines, and an explicit statement that the migration is UNAPPLIED.
